name: jump-select-demo
notes: The tier-2 JumpSolve doorway (ADR-0328) behind the REAL owned stat_test, the JuMP twin of pyomo-solve.json. A deterministic toy source emits per-instrument cluster evidence plus a candidate deck; the owned edge test decides WHICH instruments survive; JumpBudgetedSelect (dskit/pipeline/libs/jump.py) then solves a 0/1 knapsack over the SURVIVING candidates only, inside a hard budget, in a long-lived Julia worker. The deck is rigged as in the pyomo example: NOISE carries the largest value but no edge evidence, so the gate must exclude it; among the survivors greedy-by-value takes ALPHA (9) while the optimum is BRAVO+GAMMA (12). The document plans on a machine with no Julia; RUNNING it needs julia on PATH and the julia/DskitJuMP package (the suite substitutes the Python fake worker through the node's worker_command). The toy source lives in the pyomo pack's test module, so this document plans from a repo checkout; swap that one node for your own data source to make it real.

evidence.notes: role data. Deterministic fixture: scores = instrument -> {cluster: paired improvement} (the stat test's food), candidates = [{id, cost, value}] keyed by the same instrument ids.

edge_test.notes: role stat_test, toolkit-OWNED. One-sided event-clustered bootstrap PER instrument, then one BH correction across the family; never pooled.

select.notes: role capital. The survivors wire is structural: un-gated capital refuses to plan. Only surviving ids reach the Julia program; an empty gate deploys zero WITHOUT starting the worker; the reported outlay can never exceed budget (post-solve assertion, refused by name). The solver name's shape is checked at plan; whether the Julia environment provides it is checked at run.
